$description: The Encryptor file container, the one every driver reads and writes so a file encrypted on one OS decrypts on the other two. It is OpenSSL's `enc` envelope: the 8 ASCII bytes `Salted__`, an 8-byte random salt, then AES-256-CBC with PKCS#7 padding. Key (32 bytes) and IV (16 bytes) are the first 48 bytes of PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 password and the salt. macOS runs `openssl enc` (Encryptor.app/Contents/Resources/encryptor_convert.sh), Linux the private runtime's openssl, Windows the CNG primitives (windows/apps/encryptor). Vectors: _shared/tests/corpus/encryptor/vectors.json. `mime_type` is the type Linux registers for `encrypted_extension`, whose default opener the Encryptor is.
